rationale_overall: This week's pool was dominated by noise rather than genuine catalysts: junior uranium explorers (Snow Lake, Blue Sky Uranium, F4 Uranium, Stallion Uranium) are thinly-traded TSX-V/OTCQB penny stocks with no US liquidity; SpaceX and Blue Origin coverage (launches, satellite loss, Air Force rocket-cargo pause) involves private companies with no investable ticker; Yamaha's robotics division and Luminous's robotics-for-construction funding are foreign or solar-tied (excluded sector) and not clean US wave plays; Zaporizhzhia plant alerts and Taiwan's nuclear referendum are geopolitical risk events, not SMR/nuclear investment catalysts, and named no US nuclear ticker; the missile-defense cluster (Aegis BMD contract, THAAD deployments, Yemen/Israel intercepts, Russia-Ukraine drone barrage) is routine defense-news volume without a new inflection strong enough to displace a current holding; and the newly-launched HUMN humanoid-robotics ETF is an interesting robotics-wave vehicle but too fresh to clear the listing-history guardrail and not clearly stronger than any incumbent AI holding this week. AI-chip export-curb chatter (Malaysia/Thailand) is a supply-chain risk note on NVDA, already held, not a new name. With no rising-wave vehicle clearly outclassing AAPL, GOOGL, MSFT, or NVDA, and the swap bar requiring a genuine catalyst, the watchlist holds unchanged this period.
